output.brief:
Please don't approve the plan. The new CDN is not the cause; the smart-TV app update is.

About two hours after the CDN cutover finished on 9 Oct, Kestria became the first market to get smart-TV app 5.2, which makes video start sooner by buffering less. Staff testing beforehand showed 5.7% stalling versus 0.6% on the old version, on the old CDN; a QA ticket was deferred.

Since then, 5.2 TVs stall about 6% of viewing time on every ISP, while 5.1 TVs, web, iOS and Android on the same new CDN and ISPs stay at 0.6–0.7%. The handball launch came after the jump and shows no match-night effect.

I'm about 90% sure of the cause. Whether buffering drove October's cancellations is unproven; the 1 October price rise fits too.

Next:
1. Switch Kestria's TV setting back to the 5.1 values (about an hour, no new build); confirm stalls fall.
2. Hold the all-markets rollout planned for 20 Nov, just days away.
3. Don't send the breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic; keep the alert on.
4. Add app-version breakdowns to the dashboard and alerts.
5. Check the exit survey before any win-back offer.
